## jig v0.2.0-alpha.5

Channel tiers. Every new channel is end-to-end encrypted unless it is created as `public`, and
`jig` says which wherever it shows a channel. New channels reach other servers only by a
share, and the servers that carry an encrypted channel hold its ciphertext and never read it.
Channels the legacy relay already carries keep syncing for now; share them to move them onto a
contract.

Channel tiers ship as one bundle: #367, #372, #374, #339, #368, #370, #373 and #378 (JEP-0014).

This is an alpha. Pre-1.0 releases make no wire, receipt or storage compatibility guarantee, and
jig has not had an external security audit yet (D27).

### Breaking: channel tiers (JEP-0014)

- **Every new channel has a tier, fixed when it is created:** `private`, `server`, `shared` or
  `public`. The first three are end-to-end encrypted (MLS), so the server operator cannot read
  them. `public` is plaintext and readable by anyone, the operator included; `jig` labels it
  wherever it shows it, and asks the creator to confirm before creating one.
- **Upgrade jig before creating channels.** An older client's plaintext `open` create is
  refused (`UNKNOWN_TIER`). An older client can read a `public` channel but cannot post to it
  (`TIER_UNSUPPORTED`), because it cannot show the label.
- **New channels are `private` unless you choose otherwise.** `jig channel create` without
  `--tier` creates a `private` channel, whose members are added by its owner. For a team
  channel that members join themselves, use `jig channel create --tier server --join guest`.
  A `server` or `shared` channel that lets guests join admits any key the server admits,
  `--anon` session keys included.
- **Members join `server` and `shared` channels themselves** (#378). A caller whose server
  role meets the channel's `--join` setting adds itself with an MLS external commit; no admin
  has to add it, and the server holds no group secret.
- **A 1:1 stays a pair** (#374). A `#dm/` channel takes only its two members
  (`DM_IS_A_PAIR`). To bring in a third person, create a group from it with
  `jig channel create --from-dm <dm>`; the 1:1 goes on unchanged. A legacy DM that already has
  three or more members takes no further adds.
- **`jig chat` shows the tier before it sends.** In a `public`, frozen or unencrypted channel
  it refuses to send while the terminal is too small to show the tier label.
- **A channel's tier never changes.** `jig channel promote` is refused (`TIER_FIXED`): make a
  new channel instead.
- **Existing plaintext `open` channels become read-only on upgrade.** Their history stays
  readable to whoever could read it, and new posts are refused (`CHANNEL_FROZEN`). The
  operator could already read that history, so the channel is not converted in place. Its
  owner can continue it in a new encrypted channel with
  `jig channel create --successor-of <channel>`; no history moves. The server's own open
  `#jig/` system channels stay writable, as `public`.

### Breaking: how channels reach other servers

- **A channel crosses servers only by a share.** A `channel-create` relayed by a peer over the
  legacy relay is no longer taken as a channel of the receiving server (#368), so a new
  channel reaches a peer only once it is shared.
  - **New: `jig channel share <slug> <server-did> --grant read|write|member`** and
    **`jig channel unshare <slug> <server-did>`** (#339) offer and withdraw a channel. The
    other server's operator accepts with `jig-server contracts accept <offer-id>`, unless its
    peer entry for this server says `offers = "accept"`. Followers read a shared channel by
    its id, which `jig channel share` prints.
  - `shared` channels cross by contract, and are offered only to peers that implement tiers
    (#373). A follower carries their encrypted content as ciphertext and never reads it.
  - `private` and `server` channels never leave the server that orders them.
  - `public` channels do not federate automatically yet. Their owner can share one by
    contract. Automatic offers to every peer come with public channels on contracts (JEP-0014
    rule 37).
  - When a share ends, members reached through that follower are not removed automatically
    yet. Until a member's home server is recorded,
    `jig channel members <channel> --via <server-did>` lists the members whose latest write
    that server relayed, and `jig channel kick` removes them.
- **Every `channel-create` names the server that orders it** (`sequencer`). One without it is
  refused (`SEQUENCER_REQUIRED`); one naming another server is refused (`NOT_SEQUENCER`).
- **`federation.naively_accept_peer_relayed_creates` is for tests only.** With it set, a server
  stores a copy of each channel a peer creates, as releases up to v0.2.0-alpha.4 did, but
  clients refuse to read the copy, because its creation block names another server. It is
  listed among the unsafe options. Servers that trust each other set `offers = "accept"` in
  their peer entries and share channels with `jig channel share`.

### Upgrade notes

- **A follower whose copy refused the owner's records** ("does not carry channel … for
  <owner>"). This happens when the old relay gave the follower its own copy of a channel the
  owner created. Upgrade the follower and restart it; the owner does nothing. At boot the
  follower sets each such copy aside (accepting a share does the same from then on), and logs
  `set aside relayed copies of channels this server follows` with a count, plus one line per
  channel. Nothing is deleted: the copy is kept, its follower-signed records move to
  `quarantined_records`, and the owner's records then land the channel in the owner's order.
  Posts the follower's own users made in the copy, and that the owner never took, stay in the
  copy only. New copies are no longer made (#368).
- **A shared channel that stops at one post.** This happens when two servers each had their own
  channel of the same name, such as `#general`, and were peered before the share. The old relay
  landed one server's posts in the other's channel (#357), and the carried channel waits at the
  first such post. This release does not prevent it for channels peered before the share, and
  there is no safe repair in place. To confirm it, run, as the `jig` user,
  `jig-server --config /etc/jig/config.toml contracts list`: it ends with a
  `stalled: channel <id> stalled at seq <n>: block <cid> is held in channel <id>` line, and the
  log repeats `a carried channel is stalled`. You can leave it (the carried channel shows
  everything up to the stall), or end the share, either with
  `jig-server --config /etc/jig/config.toml contracts end <offer-id>`, run as `jig` on either
  side, or with `jig channel unshare` by the owner. What was carried stays readable. Before
  sharing, check that the peer has no channel of its own with that name. `deploy/README.md`,
  "A stalled carried channel", has the details.

### Fixes

- **A follower's user posts to a carried channel by its id** (#370, fixes #363):
  `jig send --channel <id>` on a follower now reaches the owner, for an encrypted `shared`
  channel too under a `write` grant (#373). This removes alpha.4's known limitation.

### Dependencies

- **wasmtime 50.0.1** (#380), with the wasm-tools crates jig uses directly (`wasmparser`,
  `wit-parser`, `wit-component`) kept in lockstep at 0.261, the release wasmtime 50 itself uses.
  50.0.1 is the patched release on the 50 line for RUSTSEC-2026-0422, -0423 and -0424, which
  alpha.4 fixed with 49.0.5 (#383).
- **Building from source needs Rust 1.97 or later**, wasmtime 50's floor (`rust-version` was
  1.95). If you build with Rust 1.95 or 1.96, upgrade first. Release binaries are built with the
  pinned toolchain, 1.99.
- **Render receipts name the new engine.** They carry wasmtime 50.0.1 and a new engine config
  fingerprint. Fuel costs are unchanged and `FUEL_SCHEDULE_VERSION` stays 0.2.0, so a receipt's
  fuel numbers are the same as before.

### Known limitations

- **Stop jig-server before re-running install.sh to upgrade.** The installer replaces the
  binaries but leaves a running server on the old build. Stop it first with
  `kill $(cat ~/.jig/jig-server.pid)` (or `$JIG_HOME/jig-server.pid` if you set `JIG_HOME`),
  then install. A later release restarts it for you (#334).
- **A shared channel whose slug matches one of the follower's own channels** cannot be used by
  its slug from a client on that follower: the slug reads the follower's own channel, with no
  error, because the client keys pins and group state by slug per server. Name the shared
  channel by its id instead (#388).
- **A shared channel peered before its share can stall** at a post the old relay carried
  between same-named channels; see Upgrade notes.

### Threat-register entries mitigated

Statuses are as of this release. *Partial* means part of the entry's decision is implemented;
the register says which part.

| Entry | What this release does | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OP-05 Content disclosure | Every new channel is end-to-end encrypted unless created as `public`, which is labelled; a follower carries a `shared` channel as ciphertext (#367, #372, #373) | Partial |
| OP-09 Federation abuse | A relayed `channel-create` naming another server is refused, and a channel reaches a peer only by a share (#368, #339) | Partial |

Still open or accepted in this release, among others: OP-04 (metadata), OP-10 and AB-05 (Sybil
resistance), AB-06 (provable abuse in encrypted channels), and NS-03. The register lists them all.
